x: वह अपना काम अनुशासन से करता है।

ety.text: Borrowed from Sanskrit अनुशासन (anuśāsana), equivalent to अनु- (anu-, “with, along”) + शासन (śāsan, “law, order”).
Inherited from Sanskrit उच्छलति (ucchalati) (compare उच्चलति (uccalati)). Cognate with Punjabi ਉੱਛਲਣਾ (ucchalṇā) / اُچّھَلݨا (ucchalṇā), Gujarati ઊછળવું (ūchaḷvũ), Marathi उसळणे (usaḷṇe).
Borrowed from Arabic قَاصِد (qāṣid). Compare English cossid.

s.g: Kyrgyzstan (a country in Central Asia, bordering on Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan and China)

x: कुम्हार ने प्यारा सा बासन मिट्टी से बनाया।

ety.text: Inherited from Prakrit 𑀓𑀼𑀁𑀪𑀆𑀭 (kuṃbhaāra), from Sanskrit कुम्भकार (kumbhakāra, “potter”). Doublet of कुंभकार (kumbhkār).

s.g: a title of the supreme being
honorary title prefixed to personal names
title given to leaders of the Vallabhan community

ety.text: Inherited from Sanskrit गोस्वामिन् (gosvāmin). Doublet of गोस्वामी (gosvāmī).
Perhaps from Sanskrit चर्पट (carpaṭa) or चपट (capaṭa) undergoing dentalization. Both are borrowed from Dravidian. Compare Marathi चापट (cāpaṭ).

s.g: Czech Republic, Czechia (a country in Central Europe)

ety.text: Inherited from Old Hindi छब्बीस (chabbīsa), from Sauraseni Prakrit 𑀙𑀯𑁆𑀯𑀻𑀲𑀁 (chavvīsaṃ), from Ashokan Prakrit 𑀲𑀟𑀼𑀯𑀻𑀲𑀢𑀺 (saḍuvīsati), from Sanskrit षड्विंशति (ṣaḍviṃśati).

s.g: to spread one's knowledge; to gossip, spread rumor
a transliteration of the English surname Trump

ety.text: Borrowed from English Trump. Cognate with Assamese ট্ৰাম্প (trampo), Bengali ট্রাম্প (ṭrampo)
Borrowed from Classical Persian طاس (tâs, “dice”). Cognate with Bengali তাস (taś), Nepali तास (tās), Punjabi ਤਾਸ਼ (tāś) / تاش (tāś).

s.g: Tel Aviv (a city in Israel that later merged with Jaffa to form Tel Aviv-Yafo)

x: जब मैं बड़ा हूँगा, मुझे द्वैभाषिक होना है।

ety.text: Sanskritic formation from द्वि- (dvi-) + भाषा (bhāṣā) + -इक (-ik). For the length of the first vowel, see the usage notes of -इक (-ik). Related to द्विभाषी (dvibhāṣī), दुभाषी (dubhāṣī), दुभाषिया (dubhāṣiyā).

s.g: to go into intoxication state of opium(पीनक)

ety.text: Unknown; potentially from बँटना (bãṭnā, “to be divided, distributed”) + -उआ (-uā), or compare Bhojpuri बटुआ (baṭuā, “metal dish”). Cognate with Punjabi ਬਟੂਆ (baṭūā).

s.g: to sprinkle, strew, dust (a powdered substance)
x: सलाद पर थोड़ा नमक बुरक दो।

ety.text: Derived from Ashokan Prakrit *𑀩𑀽𑀭 (*būra, “powder”) + Middle Indo-Aryan -𑀓𑁆𑀓- (-kka-) + -ना (-nā, verbal suffix). Doublet of बूर (būr, “chaff, husk; sawdust”), बूरा (būrā, “coarse sugar”), बुरकी (burkī, “a pinch (of salt etc.)”), and बुरबुराना (burburānā, “to sprinkle”). Platts, however, derives it from metathesis of an unattested *बुकरना (bukarnā), an alternative form of बुकटना (bukaṭnā, “to be clawed, scratched”), which is a rare or unused intransitive form of बकोटना (bakoṭnā, “to claw, scratch”).

Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *méǵh₂s Proto-Indo-Iranian *maȷ́ʰā́ Sanskrit महा- (mahā-) Proto-Indo-European *meh₁treh₂ Sanskrit मात्रा (mātrā) Sanskrit मात्र (mātra) Sanskrit महामात्र (mahāmātra) Ashokan Prakrit 𑀫𑀳𑀸𑀫𑀸𑀢 (mahāmāta) Prakrit महामत्त (mahāmatta) Hindi महावत Inherited from Prakrit महामत्त (mahāmatta), from Ashokan Prakrit 𑀫𑀳𑀸𑀫𑀸𑀢 (mahāmāta), from Sanskrit महामात्र (mahāmātra), from महा- (mahā-) + मात्र (mātra).
Hypercorrection of रिवाज (rivāj), from Classical Persian رواج (rawāj), from Arabic رَوَاج (rawāj).

s.g: to kick out, throw out, expel

ety.text: From Prakrit लत्तिअ (lattia) + आना (ānā). Compare लात (lāt, “kick”).
